headline: Mechanistic network models tie circuit architecture to bursting and feature binding
label: Mechanistic Models Of Neural Circuits
summary: Bottom-up circuit models now resolve how bursting, synchrony, and hierarchical feature binding arise from connectivity and dynamics.
synthesis: The common thread is bottom-up mechanistic simulation, in which emergent dynamics are traced to explicit network architecture rather than assumed at the component level. A four-cell central pattern generator model shows that bursting appears only once the cells are assembled into a network, with GPU parameter sweeps and symbolic encoding used to map dynamical regimes. In silico C. elegans modeling on the structural connectome infers functional communities, with electrical synapses shaping them and behavioral circuits differing in how they relate to structural and functional connectivity. A spiking model of the primate ventral visual pathway attributes hierarchical shape-feature binding to polychrony-based circuits that remain robust to Poisson input. A neural-astrocyte architecture extends this logic to reinforcement learning, where astrocytes support evidence accumulation and context switching via a hybrid automaton. What is new is the framing of glial and assembly-level mechanisms as explicit components of network computation.
